issue_context.title: [FastifyInstance] Expose `fastify#setGenReqId`
comments: Yeah, it should. I think it will be the key benefit of it
I would request that the documentation highlight the potential use case for the method.
I thought about it. it makes sense, e.g. in cases, you have a webhook endpoint and want to use the provided webhook-id as request id just for that specific endpoint.

review_comments: Can you add a tests where a `plugin` alters the `genReqId` of the parent?

Do we want the `plugin` to alter the `genReqId` of parent? Added test for opposite [here](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/5259/commits/11a42ea0a87c13dba1dacdc52f535d08564e769b#diff-c59d02cf0c0d124c85b50aa4a031acfb2d5e176b9a8be295b90125929d64bd1bR335) but can change this if we want `plugin` to update `parent.genReqId`

It should actually not alter the parent?! 
@metcoder95 please clarify ;)

haha, yeah to alter the parent. The test you point out tests when creating a new encapsulated context, which it **should not alter the parent**.
But, for plugins that does not create a new encapsulated context, they usually **seek to alter the parent context**
@metcoder95 add in test to set on root scope using fastify-plugin. Had to rework some of changes to get this test to past
Maybe add one more level of encapsulation?
